# vk v0.5.0

Date: 2026-10-26. Status: Experimental development release.
Cargo package: `vkrust` version `0.5.0+1.4.365`. Rust library/import: `vk`. License: MIT.

## Scope

Generated borrowed construction is now the default way shown to prepare native
Vulkan records. Free functions and wrapper methods continue to use the same
cached PFNs and canonical operation bodies. The pinned registry and coverage of
all 842 selected command spellings, including core Vulkan 1.0–1.4, are unchanged.

## Changes

- Add 4,959 fieldwise setters and two reviewed parallel-array setters on the
  existing records, including C strings, nested records and unambiguous slices.
  Slice setters check native count conversion; reviewed parallel arrays check
  matching lengths before changing fields.
- Generate 769 typed chain-node implementations and 1,267 XML extension
  relationships. `push_next` borrows one compatible node exclusively, checks
  canonical headers and rejects an already-linked inserted node without walking
  arbitrary raw pointers.
- Propagate lifetimes through 1,554 affected records and aliases, including
  native PFN and operation signatures. Retain native representations, field
  order, names, raw-pointer access and explicit native destruction.
- Add descriptor payload recipes that clear conflicting pointer/count choices,
  generated record contracts and external positive/negative borrow-checker
  fixtures. Keep native header helper names and generated item spacing.
- Present borrowed construction with both calling styles in the README and
  compiled crate introduction, including an output feature-chain example.

## Compatibility and migration

Use `vk = { package = "vkrust", version = "0.5" }`. The package suffix
`+1.4.365` identifies pinned Vulkan headers, not a minimum driver version.
Rust 1.98.1 and edition 2024 remain the declared baseline. Library loading is
enabled by default; the work-in-progress allocator remains opt-in.

This minor release changes Rust source compatibility. Stored borrowed records
may need `Type<'a>` annotations. Use struct-update literals with
`..Default::default()` to initialize the hidden lifetime marker. Records that
retain exclusive chain borrows, and their by-value containers, no longer
implement `Copy` or `Clone`. Build fresh array elements with
`std::array::from_fn` and borrow single records with `std::slice::from_ref`.
`AccelerationStructureGeometryDataKHR` uses `ManuallyDrop` for non-Copy union
members. Native ABI layout remains independently checked.

Keep backing storage live through a record's last use. Inspect an output chain
node after the root's final use. Links remain written; host record destruction
does not unlink nodes, destroy Vulkan objects, submit work or wait.

## Verification and limits

The implementation checkpoint passed 3,170 Rust tests/doctests, including 1,536
generated record contracts and seven external compile-fail fixtures, plus 33
Python tooling tests. Strict Clippy, deterministic generation, XML ordering,
minimal/default configurations, warnings-denied rustdoc and native-name search
checks pass. Independent C/Rust checks cover 1,447 records, 9,267 layout/value
checks and 348 bitfield byte comparisons. All 842 Rust PFN prototypes and 775
C prototypes pass; 67 protected C prototypes remain unqualified by that header
set. Native Haswell/Mesa instance/device smoke tests pass using borrowed setters.

The release pipeline verifies the actual sanitized commit, extracted Cargo
archive, independent consumers, hosted Windows/macOS tests, pinned C and VMA
oracles, and explicit Lavapipe workloads. Consult the actual workflow and
release artifacts for those release-specific results.

Borrowing covers host record storage. Public raw fields, pointer-array pointees,
opaque payloads, ambiguous lengths and unreviewed output helpers retain caller
obligations. Device/resource ownership, asynchronous completion and Vulkan valid
usage remain unsafe contracts. The allocator is not VMA-equivalent. Physical
Vulkan 1.3/1.4, WSI, video, ray tracing and broader cross-device qualification
remain open. Miri and comparative performance are not claimed. See
[qualification and limitations](../qualification.md).

## Distribution

The release tag is `v0.5.0`; the complete registry version is
`0.5.0+1.4.365`. Private/public histories have independent commit IDs. Public
source excludes private engineering documents and configuration. The pipeline
publishes the verified Cargo archive, checks registry/downloaded bytes, and
attaches API documentation, checksums and build evidence to the GitHub
development release. Existing tags and registry versions remain immutable.
